newsitem.title: UK: Hard landing injects caution into U.K. gas market.
newsitem.headline: Hard landing injects caution into U.K. gas market.

text.p: The U.K. gas market was subdued on Monday, with traders treading cautiously the day after the Network Code made its hard landing.
"It's come in with more of a whimper than a bang," said one producer.

The hard landing, introduced on Sept 1, imposes financial penalties on shippers if their offtake from the Transco- operated National Transmission System (NTS) is not matched by inputs on a a daily basis.
Traders balanced their positions in a last minute flurry of trades late on Friday and over the weekend, dealers said.
Traders said the market looked balanced on Monday, possibly leaning towards the long side.
"I'd say that people may have overcompensated for the hard landing. They have prepared themselves for the peak so there are more that are long than are short," said one.
Monday's cash out price on the flexibility market was 12.66 pence a therm (p/th).
The flex market is where Transco buys and sells gas when the NTS is out of balance, and hence a reflection of the financial penalties imposed on shippers out of balance in the system.
"At that price I would rather have been long than short," said a trader for a regional electricity company.
As expected, the hard landing brought more talk on day-ahead gas, but no trades were seen with bids heard at 13.9 p/th and an offers as high as 16 p/th.
Transco reported no operational problems on the second day of the new regime.
"The operational systems are working adequately," said Graham Ryott, the company's gas trading support manager.
Some traders already have experience of daily balancing.
"Some of the power station contracts we had last winter were more onerous on daily balancing than the Network Code," said one.
But for others it was a new requirement.
"I think we're finding it more challenging to keep our inputs and outputs balanced," said a dealer for a major shipper.
